GENERAL HEADQUARTERS
SUPREME COMMANDER FOR THE ALLIED POWERS
AG 072 (8 Apr 49) CPC/OD
(SCAPIN-1990/5)
APO 500
1 December 1950
MEMORANDUM FOR : JAPANESE GOVERNMENT.
SUBJECT : Procedures for Restoration of Patents, Utility Models, Designs and Trade-Marks to Allied Nationals
1. Reference is made to the following memoranda for the Japanese Government from General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers:
a. File AG 072 (8 Apr 49) CPC/FP, SCAPIN 1990, 8 April 1949, subject, “Procedures for Restoration of Patents, Utility Models and Designs for Allied Nationals”
b. File AG 072 (8 Apr 49) CPC/FP, SCAPIN 1990/1, 16 May 1949, subject, “Procedures for Restoration of Patent Property in Japan to Allied Nationals”
c. File AG 072 (9 Sep 49) CPC/FP, SCAPIN 2042, 9 September 1949, subject, “Trade-Marks, Trade Names and Marking of Merchandise in Japan”
d. File AG 072 (8 Apr 49) CPC/FP, SCAPIN 1990/3, 21 March 1950, subject, “Procedures for Restoration of Patents, Utility Models, and Designs to Allied Nationals”
e. File AG 072 (9 Sep 49) CPC/FP, SCAPIN 2042/1, 2 May 1950, subject, “Trade-Marks, Trade Names and Marking of Merchandise in Japan”
f. File AG 072 (8 Apr 49) CPC/OD, SCAPIN 1990/4, 4 August 1950, subject, “Procedures for Restoration of Patents, Utility Models, and Designs to Allied Nationals.”
2. The Japanese Government is directed to take necessary action to complete processing of all pending requirements pertaining to restoration, revalidation and extension of patent property and trade-marks and to deliver to the Office of the Civil Property Custodian, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers the papers and documents required thereby within thirty (30) days from the date of this memorandum. Similar requirements forwarded to the Patent Agency subsequent to the date of this memorandum will be processed and the required papers and documents submitted to the Office of the Civil Property Custodian, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers within thirty (30) days from the date of receipt by the Patent Agency.
3. Action directed in paragraph 2 above has become necessary as a result of delays encountered in the past and because of the approaching closing date of 1 February 1951 for the patent property and trade-mark restoration program.
FOR THE SUPREME COMMANDER:
K.B.BUSH
Brigadier General, USA
Adjutant General
